items.title: Bitcoin ETF Outflows Signal Market Caution Despite Price Stability
points: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $635.6 million in a single day on October 23, the largest single-day outflow of the month, reversing a three-day $1.07 billion inflow streak.
October's net flow flipped to a loss of about $176 million.
Ethereum ETFs shed another $110.6 million, bringing October ETF outflows to $1.18 billion.
Bitcoin price held flat around $81,700 despite the outflows, suggesting a 'wait-and-see mode' rather than panic selling.
Analysts link the muted price action to traders awaiting the Federal Reserve meeting on October 27-28, where rates are expected to stay unchanged.

items.title: Regulatory and Technical Security Developments
points: New York Attorney General Letitia James is seeking $1.37 billion in restitution from collapsed crypto platform NovaTech's founders, who allegedly used prayer groups and community trust to lure victims into the scheme.

Ethereum delayed its Hoodi testnet fork after security firm ChainSecurity found flaws in planned gas mechanism changes (gas is the fee structure for executing transactions) that could trap smart contracts in failed states, with 13 real-world vulnerable cases identified.
Bitcoin Core updated its security disclosure policy to address vulnerabilities that AI systems can now find in a single prompt, adapting to AI-assisted security analysis threats.

items.title: Franklin Templeton's Dividend-to-Bitcoin ETFs
points: Franklin Templeton launched two new ETFs that pair traditional U.S. stock exposure with Bitcoin in a single fund.
Every dividend paid by the underlying stocks is automatically reinvested to buy additional Bitcoin rather than being paid out to shareholders.
The strategy lets investors maintain stock market exposure while systematically accumulating Bitcoin through dividend yields.

items.title: Bitcoin Network Hashrate Milestone
points: Bitcoin's hashrate (the total computational power securing the network) hit its highest level in seven months.
Higher hashrate means more miners are competing to validate transactions, strengthening network security and making attacks more costly.

points: 1. U.S. spot Bitcoin funds experienced their largest single-day outflow of October with $635.6 million exiting on Thursday, reversing a three-day $1.07 billion inflow streak.
2. The outflow flipped October's balance to a net loss of approximately $176 million, while Ethereum ETFs contributed an additional $110.6 million in October outflows totaling $1.18 billion.
3. Bitcoin maintained a flat price at $81,700 despite the large fund withdrawals, indicating market participants are holding positions steady rather than panic selling.
4. Analysts attribute the muted price action to traders entering a holding pattern ahead of the Federal Reserve meeting October 27-28, where rates are expected to remain unchanged.
